key_insight: A two-stage diffusion model reproduces branching ribs followed by pore-forming bridges through a switch in how local flux drives growth.
engineering_relevance: The framework links diffusion-driven material deposition to density-based topology optimization, offering a route to simulate evolving porous architectures on a fixed finite element mesh.
method: Represent material with a density field on an active layer of a fixed finite element mesh.
Stage 1: promote dendritic growth where a local diffusive-flux stimulus exceeds a threshold.
Stage 2: invert the stimulus so high local flux suppresses precipitation and stabilizes pores.
evidence_signal: A reference calculation produces approximately uniformly spaced pores absent near domain edges, qualitatively consistent with diatom valve observations.
watch_item: Quantitative validation against cryo-electron tomography is proposed rather than demonstrated in the abstract.
paper_title: A two-stage diffusion-driven morphogenesis model with evolving connectivity
